rv.q: This blast of undiluted teen spirit is guaranteed to leave you feeling windblown, hyped up and ready to race through the most torpid summer night.

Lines like "we are not strangers" and "the world is an orphanage for grown-ups" now stick out as thematic indicators. Being a runaway, however real it remains at Covenant House, is halfway toward metaphor at City Center, where even garden-variety alienation (or mere theatermania) counts as a rough childhood.
The large, multiethnic cast is appropriately young and raw, giving an air of powerful authenticity to the material.
